directions.pos: Turn the subject 20–30° away from you so the light models one side of the face.
directions.exp: Easiest light to expose; expose for skin, keep zebras off cheeks and white clothes.

directions.pos: Stand so the light comes from one side; place a white wall, card or dupatta on the shadow side.
directions.exp: Expose for the lit side of the face; let the far side fall softly darker — don't chase shadow detail with ISO.

directions.pos: Put the sun or window behind the subject, just out of frame or hidden by the head; shoot from slightly low.
directions.exp: Expose for the face (Face Priority on); let the background and hair rim glow and clip softly.

directions.pos: Move people into open shade or under a canopy; for landscapes and buildings, shoot strong shapes and shadows.
directions.exp: Expose for the brightest important surface; deep shadows are fine — lifting them only adds noise.

directions.pos: Step closer so the subject fills more of the frame, or change angle to put a darker background behind them.
directions.exp: Spot-meter the face and lock it (AEL); accept a white background rather than a dark face.

directions.pos: Lower the horizon in the frame, or include less sky; wait for clouds over the sun.
directions.exp: Expose for the foreground; the Knee holds the sky. Never darken the whole photo to save the sky.

directions.pos: Move the subject so the face is fully in sun or fully in shade — no spots on the face.
directions.exp: Expose for the face area only; if spots remain, wait for a passing cloud.

directions.pos: Subject 1–2 m from the window at 45°, camera with its back to the side wall; switch room lights off.
directions.exp: Expose for the window-side cheek; the room behind can go darker naturally.

directions.pos: Ask the subject to lift the chin or face a lamp or window; avoid standing directly under a tube.
directions.exp: Expose for the eyes; if eye sockets go dark, move the light source, not the ISO.

directions.d: Lamp or diya behind the subject
directions.pos: Place the light slightly to the side, not straight behind; use a second lamp or white wall in front.
directions.exp: Expose for the face, not the flame — flames and bulbs may clip.

checklist.b: 1 Open aperture  2 Slower shutter to the Min. SS (SteadyShot On)  3 Move closer to the light / add a lamp  4 ISO last, never above the row's cap.
Exposure Comp. stays at 0 or above, except deliberate silhouettes.
When ISO reaches its cap, the camera slows the shutter instead of underexposing — brace yourself or rest the camera.
Tube, LED, neon: mode S at 1/100 (1/50 when dim or if the scale blinks). In mode A the camera may go faster and band.
1600 for clean files. 3200 only for diya, candle, dim-lamp, blue-hour and night rows — rest the camera instead of going higher.
High ISO NR Normal · Shading Comp. Off · DRO Off · Silent Shooting Off.
Histogram right side near the edge, not hitting it. Zebras read the JPEG — at 100+ the RAW still has about 2/3 stop to spare.

The light on your subject: quality + source (e.g. Haze / smog · golden hour). Two rows fit? Take the one lighting the face; if still unsure, the one with the higher Exposure Comp.
White Balance › C.Temp./Filter · ISO AUTO Max · Metering Mode · recipe idea.
Your genre: aperture and Focus Mode · Area. Landscape, architecture, silhouette in daylight: ISO max 400.

rules.b: Zebras read brightness. Strong reds, oranges, yellows and magentas clip in one colour channel first — press DISP in playback for the R/G/B histograms. A channel touching the right edge → Exposure Comp. one step down (never below 0).
Single bloom: F2.8–4 (F1.8 leaves only part of a petal sharp at 0.4 m). Beds: F4–5.6. Background blur for beds: F1.8 and step back.
E 50mm F1.8 OSS focuses to 0.39 m. Closer? Step back and crop in post — never force it.
1/250 or faster; wait for the pause between gusts and shoot a burst of 3.
Find a shaded or dark background behind a lit flower — it makes colour glow without raising exposure.
Swap M1 to Recipe 21 (Marigold Gold) in Nov–Jan; to 22 (Rose Velvet) in Feb rose season. Keep the rest of the plan.
